newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FIRST BSE CASE FOUND IN NETHERLANDS.
newsitem.headline: FIRST BSE CASE FOUND IN NETHERLANDS.

text.p: The Netherlands on Friday reported its first case of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease.
"I have the worst news that any agriculture minister can have," Dutch farm minister Jozias van Aartsen told Dutch television.
"The Netherlands was until now an island free of this disease. With great regret I have to announce that this is no longer the case."
A ministry spokesman confirmed that this was the first case of the brain-wasting disease to be identified in The Netherlands.
Piet van Dijk told Reuters that the pregnant cow, which had been born in The Netherlands five years ago and had never been out of the country, was identified as contaminated on March 11.

He said that the entire herd at the farm in Wilp in the central Netherlands, comprising 60 dairy cows and 50 calves would be slaughtered on Saturday as a precautionary measure and their remains examined for possible contamination.
Van Aartsen said he had contacted European Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler and some of his European Union colleagues to keep them informed of developments.
The Dutch meat commodities board said that all cattle for slaughter are rigorously checked by independent veterinary experts on arrival at abattoirs.
"It is absolutely impossible" that any BSE-contaminated animal would be slaughtered for consumption, the Dutch ANP news agency quoted a spokesman as saying.

Since the initial discovery of the disease in 1986, some 178,000 BSE cases have been confirmed in the European Union and Switzerland, according to European Commission figures. Up to the end of last year, the vast majority of cases were in Britain.
